name: FreeSSL.org
titleTag: FreeSSL.org alternative for Let's Encrypt | docstoc
metaDescription: Compare FreeSSL.org with docstoc: plans, ACME and API access against Let's Encrypt DV issued with one DNS TXT record. Facts and limits.
headline: FreeSSL.org or docstoc: ACME tooling or a managed Let's Encrypt workflow
sub: Both give you free-to-start HTTPS certificates: FreeSSL.org leans on ACME and a REST API, docstoc on one DNS record and a workspace.
whatItIs: FreeSSL.org describes itself as a free SSL certificate provider with ACME tools. At the time of writing its site lists 90-day and 1-year single-domain, multi-domain and wildcard certificates, and four plans: Free at $0 a month, Basic at $9.9, Pro at $99.9 and Enterprise on request. It says issuance takes 1 to 5 minutes, renewal is automated, and ACME integrations plus a REST API are available. It suits people who want to script certificates themselves.
whereTheyAreStronger: A REST API is listed on every plan, which helps if certificate requests are part of your own tooling.
It lists 1-year certificates as well as 90-day ones, which docstoc does not offer.
It lists a higher tier for volume: Pro at $99.9 a month and an Enterprise plan with custom solutions.
Technical support is listed on all plans, including Free.
whereDocstocFits: Free includes 5 Let's Encrypt certificates of 90 days each. Pro adds multi-SAN certificates and Business adds wildcards and higher volume.
You publish one DNS TXT record (DNS-01), download PEM files and install them on nginx, Apache, Caddy or your host panel.
Renewals are handled in the product while your plan stays active, in the same account as invoice follow-ups and documents.
Pricing is a flat Pro plan at $14.99 a month or Business at $39.99 a month, shown on the docstoc pricing page at the time of writing.

comparison.competitor: 90-day and 1-year certificates listed.
comparison.docstoc: 90-day Let's Encrypt certificates only.

comparison.competitor: Free, Basic $9.9, Pro $99.9 a month, Enterprise on request (at the time of writing).
comparison.docstoc: Free allowance of 5 certificates; Pro $14.99 and Business $39.99 a month cover SSL together with other docstoc tools.

comparison.competitor: ACME integrations and a REST API.
comparison.docstoc: Renewal inside the product; Pro includes an ACME API.

comparison.competitor: The site lists three ways to supply domain details; it does not name the CA on the page I read.
comparison.docstoc: DNS-01 with one TXT record; the CA is Let's Encrypt.

comparison.competitor: Certificate provider and ACME tools.
comparison.docstoc: Automation layer for Let's Encrypt, plus invoice chase drafts and document tools.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose FreeSSL.org if you want an API on every plan, 1-year certificates, or a dedicated certificate service with higher tiers for many domains. It fits developers who build certificate requests into their own scripts.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you already use it for invoices or documents and want HTTPS for a domain in the same account, with one TXT record and renewals handled. It stays DV only on Let's Encrypt.

faq.q: Is FreeSSL.org free?
faq.a: It has a Free plan at $0 a month, and paid Basic and Pro plans at the time of writing. Check its pricing page for the current limits.

faq.q: Which certificate authority does docstoc use?
faq.a: Let's Encrypt. docstoc is an automation layer, not a reseller or a CA, so you get DV certificates only.

faq.q: Can I move a domain from FreeSSL.org to docstoc?
faq.a: Yes. Add the hostname in docstoc, publish the TXT record, install the new PEM files, check HTTPS, then stop the old certificate. Never email a private key.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose Hostinger if your site is or will be on a Hostinger plan: SSL arrives without extra steps and you do not touch DNS for it.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if your site is on another host, a server you run or a portal on a custom domain, and you want Let's Encrypt DV with a TXT record and managed renewals.

faq.q: Is Hostinger SSL free?
faq.a: Hostinger says unlimited SSL is free with its hosting plans. You still pay for the hosting plan.

faq.q: Do I need Hostinger hosting to use docstoc SSL?
faq.a: No. docstoc works with any host where you can install PEM files and edit DNS.

faq.q: Does docstoc offer wildcard certificates?
faq.a: Yes, on the Business plan. Multi-SAN certificates are on Pro.
